newsitem.title: USA: Entergy seeks 7-yr River Bend cost recovery.
newsitem.headline: Entergy seeks 7-yr River Bend cost recovery.

text.p: Entergy Corp said Tuesday it will ask Texas regulators to approve recovery of River Bend nuclear power plant costs over seven years via a universal service charge.
It said the charge is designed to prevent cost shifting among customer classes. This charge is already included in rates, the utility pointed out.

Customers who remain connected to the Entergy system for reliability purposes, but who get power from another source, would continue to pay the charge so that costs will not be shifted to Entergy's other customers, it said.

The company said the charge is part of the Transition to Competition plan it will file with the Public Utility Commission of Texas Wednesday proposing accelerated recovery of costs associated with the River Bend nuclear plant.
There's no provision in the plan for recovering River Bend investment from customers that disconect themselves from the system, Entergy spokesman Cyril Guerrera said.
The merger agreement with Gulf States Utilities, which took effect in January of 1994, calls for a rate case to be filed in November of this year, the company noted.
Entergy chose to take this opportunity to include its Transition to Competition plan as a part of this case.

Guerrera said the Texas proposal is similar to the filing made in Arkansas last month covering investment in the Arkansas Nuclear 1 and Grand Gulf nuclear power plants; in September covering Riber Bend, Waterford 3 and other potential stranded costs; and in Mississippi in August.
The proposals are designed to achieve an orderly transition to retail electric competition, it said.
The Texas filing proposes performance standards for River Bend by setting a ceiling on operating, capital, and fuel expenses, Entergy said.

If expenses exceed the ceiling, then the company will absorb the higher costs unless caused by a catastrophic event. If expenses fall below the ceiling, then the company will benefit from those efficiencies.
The filing also includes a performance rate plan for Entergy Gulf States that has a return on equity band of 2 percent around a mid-point established by the commission.

The company said it will absorb costs or keep savings within the band. However, if costs or savings are outside of the band, then these would be shared equally with customers. -- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.
